title: Hansel and Gretel and the gingerbread house.
lines: At the edge of a big forest lived a poor woodcutter with his two children.
The boy was called Hansel, and the girl was called Gretel.
They didn't have much to eat, but they loved each other very much.
One day Hansel and Gretel went into the forest with their daddy to gather wood.
Hansel had a piece of bread in his pocket.
Along the way he dropped little crumbs on the path.
That way we'll always find our way back, he said.
Daddy chopped wood, and the children played among the trees.
They picked blackberries and watched the squirrels.
But they wandered too far away.
When they wanted to go back, they looked for the breadcrumbs.
But they were gone!
The birds had eaten them all.
Peck, peck, peck.
Oh dear, said Gretel.
Now we're lost.
They walked and walked.
It got dark.
Hoo, went the owl.
Gretel held Hansel's hand tightly.
The next morning they saw a little white bird.
It sang so beautifully, and it flew ahead of them.
Follow me!
They followed the bird, and then they saw something unbelievable.
A little house!
But not just any house.
The roof was made of cake.
The walls were made of chocolate.
The windows were made of sugar, and around the door hung sweets in every colour.
Mmm!
Hansel broke off a piece of the roof.
Gretel licked the window.
Nibble, nibble, little mouse, who is nibbling at my house?
called a voice.
The door opened, and there stood an old witch with a long nose and a crooked stick.
Come in, children, she said sweetly.
But she wasn't sweet at all.
She locked Hansel in a cage and Gretel had to clean and cook all day long.
But Gretel was clever.
She saw that the witch could hardly see.
One day the witch was in the back kitchen.
Gretel quietly took the key from the table.
Click!
She opened the cage.
Come on, Hansel, quick!
They put the witch in the cage and turned the key.
Now she can't be mean to anyone anymore, said Gretel.
In the house they found a chest full of pearls and gold.
They filled their pockets, and the little white bird led them back home.
Daddy was standing at the door.
He had been searching all night.
Hansel!
Gretel!
He hugged his children so tight.
With the pearls they bought food for the whole winter, and they were never poor again.
